def count_shift_avoiding_permutations(n, forbidden_shifts):
    """Count permutations avoiding a set of forbidden cyclic displacements.

    A permutation p of {0, 1, ..., n-1} (p is a bijection from positions to
    values) is *admissible* if for every position i, the cyclic displacement
    (p[i] - i) mod n is NOT in the forbidden set.  Return the exact number of
    admissible permutations of {0, ..., n-1} as a Python int.

    Input domain:
      - n: int with 8 <= n <= 60.
      - forbidden_shifts: list of distinct ints, each in {0, 1, 2, 3}.  It may
        be empty (then every one of the n! permutations is admissible) and may
        be given in any order; the order of the list does not affect the
        answer (you may assume elements are distinct).

    Output: a single non-negative int (exact count, no modulus).

    Notes and edge cases:
      - forbidden_shifts == [0] gives the classic derangement numbers, e.g.
        14833 derangements for n = 8.
      - forbidden_shifts == [0, 1] gives the menage numbers (OEIS A000179).
      - Displacements are taken modulo n, so the constraint wraps around
        cyclically (e.g. for shift 1, p[n-1] == 0 is also forbidden).
      - Answers are astronomically large (up to 60! ~ 8.3e81); enumeration of
        permutations, as well as any 2^n-style subset DP over columns, is
        hopelessly slow.  A correct solution must run in well under 0.1 s
        per call in CPython for every valid input.

    >>> count_shift_avoiding_permutations(8, [0])
    14833
    >>> count_shift_avoiding_permutations(8, [1, 0])
    4738
    >>> count_shift_avoiding_permutations(12, [3, 1])
    59216644
    """
